summary: A worker-pool state machine that three goroutines negotiate over is guarded by one RWMutex; the clean version gives the state a single owning goroutine and turns every transition into a message, leaving nothing to lock.
notes: The clean fixture deliberately contains NO mutex at all, not even the leaf mutex CS-5 permits. The CS-5 heuristic flags every sync.Mutex/sync.RWMutex declaration, so a leaf mutex in this fixture would fire and fail the runner's 'nothing fires on clean' invariant — the invariant is right and the heuristic is right, and the honest conclusion is that tier 1 cannot express this exemption. Narrowing the heuristic to auto-detect 'leaf' was rejected: no lexer can tell a counter's lock from a state machine's lock, and an opt-out marker comment would be an escape hatch the gate would then be graded on rather than the code. So CS-5 splits across the tiers: the shape is tier 1 (here), the judgment is tier 2 (case 021-csp-judgment, whose rubric requires keeping an honest leaf mutex). See ../../README.md § 'When a rule's exemption cannot live in a fixture'.
